summary: Decompresses block-compressed texture rows with serpentine error diffusion. For each of a4 output rows, walks the row pixels, looks up palette entries through a grid (this+0x1BC) with channel offsets (this+0x1CC, this+0x11C), populates empty palette cells via BitstreamTextureBlockCopy, writes the chosen palette index to the destination pixel, and accumulates quantization error into a dither error buffer (this+0x1C4) that drives the neighbouring pixels, alternating scan direction per row via a toggle at this+0x1C8.

Load palette channel tables: v6 = a1[29] (this+0x74) with v34 = v6[0], v7 = v6[1] (this+0x78) and v32 = v6[2] (this+0x7C); v5 = a1[23] (row pixel width, this+0x5C) drives the inner iteration.
Outer loop over a4 rows: guard a4 > 0 via the initial result = a4; maintain the source row pointer v45 = a3 and reset the error accumulators at the start of each row.

Scan-direction toggle at *(v4+36) (this+0x1C8): when set, switch to the reverse pass (v40 = -1, v52 = -3) and clear the toggle; otherwise use the forward pass (v40 = 1, v52 = 3) and set the toggle, so consecutive rows alternate direction.

Per pixel, derive three source component values (v15/v16/v54) via the channel offset table v44 (this+0x1CC) and palette base v49 (this+0x11C), index the palette grid v36 (this+0x1BC); when the grid cell is empty (0) call BitstreamTextureBlockCopy (0x0051DB31) to populate it.

Write the chosen palette index into the destination pixel *v50 and compute the per-channel quantization error from the palette tables (v34/v7/v32 at this+0x74, this+0x78, this+0x7C), accumulating diffusion terms into the error buffer v12 (pointed to by this+0x1C4) channels 0/1/2.
Inner loop over v38 pixels (this+0x5C), advancing the source/destination pointers v51/v50 and the error row v12 in the scan direction v52/v40 for each pixel.
Flush the accumulated error into the row-tail error cells after each row: *v12 = v48 (channel 0), v12[1] = v47 (channel 1), v12[2] = v46 (channel 2).
Return the last row's trailing error value v46 (16-bit) as the function result.
